subject: Different detection function values between "distance" R package and Distance software

messages.author: 5d03b2de1abe25e8
messages.subject: Different detection function values between "distance" R package and Distance software
parts:
Hi list.
I am trying to estimate the cetacean population size in Sinop. I was using "distance" R package for my analysis. Last week, I tried to do same analysis in Distance software for Windows. Surprisingly, most of the results were different. I know I am missing something but I could not figure it out. I have attached my csv file and dst file. I have conducted 4 survey in each season, so I included season as strata. Since there is no enough observation in each season, I wanted to estimate pooled detection function for all season and then estimate densities by strata.  In R, my commands were as follows;

dd_data <- read.csv2("DD_trial.csv", header = T, na.strings = "")
dd_data$Region.Label <- as.factor(dd_data$Season)
dd_data$Effort <- dd_data$Transect.Length
dd_data$Sample.Label <- dd_data$Transect
dd_data$distance <- as.numeric(dd_data$distance)
conv_factor <- convert_units("meter","meter","square kilometer")
dd_hr_SEASON <- ds(dd_data, key = "hr", convert.units = conv_factor, formula = ~ Region.Label)


And the results;
Summary for distance analysis 
Number of observations :  86 
Distance range         :  0  -  1181 

Model : Hazard-rate key function 
AIC   : 1167.34 

Detection function parameters
Scale coefficient(s):  
                     estimate        se
(Intercept)         5.4248693 0.8423755
Region.LabelSpring  0.7058745 0.8612046
Region.LabelSummer -0.4560141 0.8916823

Shape coefficient(s):  
            estimate        se
(Intercept) 0.605469 0.2372051

                       Estimate          SE        CV
Average p             0.3657354  0.06217718 0.1700059
N in covered region 235.1426562 45.31074671 0.1926947

Everything was fine until this point. Then I tried same analysis in Distance software. I choosed MCDS engine and Region Label as factor covariate, hazard-rate for key function. Anything else was default. 

Results:
       Convergence was achieved with    4 function evaluations.
       Final Ln(likelihood) value =  -582.03127    
       Akaike information criterion =   1172.0625    
       Bayesian information criterion =   1181.8799    
       AICc =   1172.5563    

As you can see, AIC values are different. Of course, p,ESW and f(0) values which are related to detection function were also different but I did not want to share all results. I've been trying to find out where I made a mistake for a week. 
It would be great, if anyone help.
Best,
Ugur

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Different detection function values between "distance" R package and Distance software
parts:
Ugur

This question is asked on the Distance list  on occasion.  Here is an answer I provided back in 2018:
> The answer is that the likelihood values are different according to the two different fitting engines.  The optimisation used to estimate the parameters of the hazard rate detection function are not the same, and for complex models, will produce slightly different estimates.  Because the hazard rate model is more complex than the half normal, the differences in the fitting algorithms are likely to be more pronounced with the hazard rate models.  This is a situation with which we are familiar and occurs in other data sets we have analysed.

The difference between results is exacerbated with the addition of the factor covariate.  Note particularly for the output from R the relative size of the point estimates and standard errors of the season factor covariates (suggesting the season effect is estimated imprecisely--there are only 5 detections in autumn).

There is nothing you have done wrong in your analysis.  However, the Distance for Windows output shows weak support for the presence of a season effect on detectability, consistent with the results from R. 

Eric Rexstad

Eric

Thank you for your quick response. I'm sorry to ask a question that has already been answered. It is my bad that I did not use the right keywords for searching.  But I have one more beginner question if you let me. The issue that led me to use the Distance Software for Windows is "distance" package throws an error when I use the dht2() function to estimate density by strata when both strat_formula and covariate are Region.Label (Season in my case). I think it is because of there is no observation of target species in the Winter season. The problem disappears when I remove the winter season from the data or when I do not use Region.Label as a covariate. Since my research question is to estimate the seasonal and annual density of animals in the region, I think I should not exclude the winter season. Or I shouldn't include the region as a covariate despite the lowest AIC value. Here is dht2() output:

dd.res <- dht2(ddf = dd_hr_SEASON, flatfile = dd_data, convert_units = conv_factor,
               strat_formula = ~ Region.Label, stratification = "replicate")
Error in predict.ds(ddf, bigdat, compute = TRUE) : 
  fields or factor levels in `newdata` do not match data used in fitted model

A similar question was asked in the past months and the answer was that the problem might be related to "droplevels()". I tried a few things but I was not successful. I do not encounter a problem when I use the same model in the Distance Software. Since I usually work in mac os environment, I prefer using R if I can overcome the problem. 
Thank you in advance for your help.
Ugur.

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Different detection function values between "distance" R package and Distance software
parts:
Ugur

Thanks for your new question and your research to see previous messages on the topic of dht2() .  Clearly, if there are no detections of the target species in winter, the density estimate for winter will be 0.

From what I remember seeing in your Distance for Windows software, there are very few detections in autumn also, and the delta-AIC score was quite small for the "season covariate" model.  Your inference is probably not going to be much different whether you use the season covariate or do not use it.

From the software perspective, you could install the Github version of the software:

remotes::install_github("DistanceDevelopment/Distance")

which includes the droplevels() fix you note.  That fix was made on 24March, whereas the CRAN release is from 31January.
